important.name: record_add fallback in the brief cannot run as instructed
important.summary:
record_section tells the agent to 'run the same heredoc with the lists filled inline and this call' (record_add). The heredoc record_heredoc builds for record_draft has no FINDINGS/STRENGTHS lists (lists defaults to ()) and its import line is derived from the call name, so it reads 'from harness_lib.review_models import record_draft'. Swapping only the call, as the brief says, raises NameError: record_add. The documented fallback for the too-long-command failure is therefore broken exactly when it is needed; test_record_section_offers_add_and_names_the_too_long_error only asserts the text is present, never runs it.

Also (overall): record_section tells the reviewer to run 'the same heredoc with the lists filled inline and this call' for record_add, but that heredoc comes from record_heredoc(ctx, record_draft call) with no lists, so its only import is 'from harness_lib.review_models import record_draft' and it defines no FINDINGS or STRENGTHS. Swapping the call yields NameError: record_add is not defined. pr-reviewer.md also says the heredoc runs as written with the path setup unchanged, so a compliant agent cannot fix the import. This is the exact path an agent takes when Write is unavailable or the draft fails. test_record_section_offers_add_and_names_the_too_long_error only asserts the call string is present, so it cannot catch this.

Also (runtime): fixer_brief renders the 'fixed' and 'cited' examples both with id M2 into one JSON skeleton under "fixed". FixReport._unique_ids raises 'issue ids recorded more than once' for that shape, so a fixer that mirrors the skeleton fails validation. The example predates this PR but now ships as a literal JSON document to copy; _draft_json's docstring also says 'one example per list' while FIXED carries two.

Also (docs): pr-reviewer.md:47-54 names record_add as the fallback when a draft is not an option, and the brief record_section emits (pr_review.py:748) 'run the same heredoc with the lists filled inline and this call'. The same heredoc is built by record_heredoc(ctx, record_draft call) with no lists, so it imports only record_draft and declares no FINDINGS/STRENGTHS: swapping in the record_add call raises NameError on record_add, and there are no lists to fill. A reviewer without Write (or past the size limit) follows the documented path into an error.
fix: Import both names in the reviewer heredoc (e.g. 'from harness_lib.review_models import record_add, record_draft') and say the record_add variant defines FINDINGS = [...] and STRENGTHS = [...] above the call.

Emit a second, complete record_add heredoc (record_heredoc(ctx, add, lists)) in the brief instead of describing an edit of the first, and add a test that runs it verbatim like test_record_heredoc_runs_verbatim.
Render a second complete fenced heredoc for the pieces path: record_heredoc(ctx, add, lists), which imports record_add and carries the FINDINGS/STRENGTHS list skeleton
Make record_heredoc import both record_draft and record_add, and spell out the FINDINGS = [...] / STRENGTHS = [...] lines the inline path needs
Extend the driver test to run the record_add heredoc in a subprocess, as the record_draft test already does
Give the cited example a different id (e.g. M5), or merge them into one entry carrying both files and no_change, and change the _draft_json docstring to 'the examples per list'.

Have record_section print a second complete heredoc for record_add (import record_add, FINDINGS = [ ... ], STRENGTHS = [ ... ] with the commented examples, then the record_add call) instead of pointing at the record_draft heredoc.
Reword the brief and pr-reviewer.md:49-50 to say: change the import to record_add and define FINDINGS and STRENGTHS lists above the call.

important.name: record_fixes_draft and draft_path run_id routing cannot fail in the unit tests
important.summary: test_draft_path_sits_in_the_run and test_record_fixes_draft pass run_id=_RUN_ID while _RUN_ID is also the run `current` names (run_repo starts it), so both pass unchanged if draft_path or record_fixes_draft drops run_id and falls back to the current run. The fixer brief heredoc (record_fixes_draft with run_id) is only substring-checked (test_pr_review_driver.py 842-845, 1302) and never executed, unlike the reviewer heredoc in test_record_heredoc_runs_verbatim. A regression would make a fixer read its draft from, and write its report to, whatever run `current` names after a newer capture.
fix: In test_record_fixes_draft, write the draft under _RUN_ID, then rm.start_run(_PR, _OTHER_RUN, repo=run_repo) before record_fixes_draft(..., run_id=_RUN_ID); assert fixes/w1_fix_1.json exists under run_dir(_PR, run_repo, _RUN_ID) and run_dir(_PR, run_repo) / 'fixes' does not exist (mirroring TestRecordRunId). Do the same in test_draft_path_sits_in_the_run so the expected path differs from the current run's drafts directory.

Alternatively add a driver test that writes a {fixed, bubbled} draft at the path the fix brief names, starts a newer run, and runs _heredoc(fix brief) in a subprocess, asserting SIGNAL: DONE and the fixes file under the brief's run.

minor.name: record_add dedup misses in-call duplicates and whitespace-variant strengths
minor.summary:
The docstring and brief promise an identical item is skipped. Findings are only checked against old.findings, so two identical findings in one call are both kept. Strengths are compared raw against stored, already-stripped strengths, so 's1 ' is not matched to 's1' and becomes a duplicate after ReviewerReport strips it.

Also (overall): Strengths are compared before normalization: an old stored 's1' and a new 's1 ' differ, so the new one is kept, then the ReviewerReport validator strips it and the report holds 's1' twice. Findings are de-duplicated only against the old report, so a finding repeated within one call is stored twice, while strengths in the same call are collapsed by dict.fromkeys. Both contradict the docstring promise that an identical item is skipped.
fix: merged = list(dict.fromkeys([*old.findings, *added])) (frozen Finding models hash) and kept = list(dict.fromkeys([*old.strengths, *(s.strip() for s in strengths)])).
Strip strengths before comparing, e.g. dict.fromkeys(s.strip() for s in strengths)
De-duplicate added findings in order (dict.fromkeys(added)) before appending them
